label: Light duty
description: Cars and light trucks combined, the way FHWA and BTS report vehicle-miles and passenger-miles since 2007. Rates for passenger cars and light trucks roll up to this class.

label: Passenger car
description: Passenger cars (FARS automobile body types, 1 to 13). FARS counts them separately, but exposure after 2006 exists only for light duty, so rates roll up to light duty.

label: Light truck
description: Light trucks: FARS utility vehicles (SUVs), van-based light trucks, light conventional (pickup) trucks and other light trucks (body types 14 to 49). FARS counts them separately, but exposure after 2006 exists only for light duty, so rates roll up to light duty.

label: Motorcycle
description: Motorcycles, mopeds, scooters and similar motored cycles, including three-wheeled ones (FARS body types 80 to 89).

label: Bus
description: Buses of all kinds (FARS body types 50 to 59).

label: Heavy truck
description: Medium and heavy trucks (FARS body types 60 to 79).

label: Light aircraft
description: Piston and electric airplanes in NTSB data, plus Part 91 airplanes with no engine record. Some of the airplanes with no engine record may be turbine aircraft.

label: Turboprop
description: Turboprop airplanes, taken from the NTSB engine type. The FAA survey reports them as Turboprop.

label: Business jet
description: Turbofan, turbojet and geared-turbofan airplanes that are not operated under Part 121 or 129. The FAA survey reports them as Turbojet.

label: Airliner
description: Turbofan or turbojet airplanes operated under Part 121 or 129, plus Part 121 or 129 airplanes with no engine record. Part 121 cargo airplanes are included.

label: Helicopter
description: Helicopters and gyroplanes in NTSB data, and rotorcraft in the FAA survey.

label: Experimental
description: Amateur-built and other experimental-certificate aircraft. NTSB marks them by the homebuilt flag, which takes precedence over engine type, so they are not counted in other aircraft classes.

label: Other
description: Vehicles that fit no named class. On the road this is FARS other vehicles such as farm and construction equipment, ATVs and snowmobiles (body types 90 to 97); in aviation it is gliders, balloons, blimps, weight-shift, powered parachutes, ultralights, powered lift and rockets.

label: Unknown
description: Vehicles whose type is not recorded. On the road this is FARS unknown body types (98 and 99).

label: Private
description: Operated for personal use rather than for hire. In NTSB data this is Part 91 personal or unrecorded use and non-U.S. non-commercial flights; on the road it is a private special use or no special use at all.

label: Commercial
description: Operated for hire or business. On the road this is buses and medium or heavy trucks, plus taxi, school-bus, other bus and similar commercial FARS special uses. In aviation it is Parts 121, 125, 129, 133, 135 and 137, Part 91K, non-U.S. commercial flights, and Part 91 business-type uses such as instruction, executive and aerial work. A government use takes precedence on the road.

label: Government
description: Operated by a public body. In NTSB data this is public-use, armed-forces and firefighting flights. On the road it is the government and emergency FARS special uses (such as military, police, ambulance and fire), which take precedence over a bus or heavy truck body type.

label: Unknown
description: Operator type not recorded or not decided by the source. In FARS this is an unknown special use.

label: Road private
description: Road vehicles with no special use or a private special use, and a body type that is not a bus or medium or heavy truck.

label: Road commercial
description: Road vehicles in commercial service. FARS decides this first from body type (all buses and medium or heavy trucks), and otherwise from commercial special uses such as taxi, school bus and other bus.

label: General aviation
description: Part 91, on-demand Part 135, Part 137 and Part 133 flying together, as the FAA General Aviation and Part 135 Activity Survey counts them. Flight hours by aircraft class exist only at this level; flight hours by Part exist without an aircraft class.

label: Part 91
description: General operating and flight rules, covering private and corporate flying, including Part 91K. Counted within general aviation; its flight hours are derived from survey use rows.

label: Part 121
description: Air carrier operations under Part 121, measured by BTS as domestic air carrier miles. Events include all-cargo flights, although the passenger-mile exposure covers passengers only.

label: Part 135
description: On-demand commuter and air taxi operations, counted within general aviation. Scheduled Part 135 service is classed separately.

label: Part 135 scheduled
description: Scheduled commuter operations under Part 135, which the FAA survey does not cover, so no exposure exists for this class.

label: Part 137
description: Agricultural aircraft operations such as crop dusting. Counted within general aviation.

label: Part 133
description: Rotorcraft external-load operations. Counted within general aviation.

label: Other
description: Regulations that are not separately classed. In NTSB data this is Parts 125, 129, 103, 107 and 437, public-use and armed-forces flights, and non-U.S. flights; road vehicles with a government or emergency special use also land here, unless a bus or heavy truck body type makes them road commercial.

label: Unknown
description: Regulation not recorded. In NTSB data this is an empty or unknown regulation profile; in FARS it is an unknown special use.

label: None
description: No mandated maintenance or inspection. No current source mapping assigns this value.

label: State inspection
description: Periodic inspection set by individual states, as for passenger vehicles. No current source mapping assigns this value.

label: Mandated periodic
description: Mandated periodic maintenance or inspection. FARS assigns it to buses and medium or heavy trucks; NTSB assigns it to Parts 91, 91K, 121, 125, 133, 135 and 137.

label: Unknown
description: Maintenance regime not determined. FARS leaves cars, light trucks, motorcycles and other body types here, and NTSB uses it for regulations without a mapped regime.

label: Aviation
description: Air transport, including airliners, general aviation and helicopters. Events come from NTSB and exposure from BTS and the FAA survey.

label: Highway
description: Road transport, including cars, trucks, buses and motorcycles. Events come from FARS and exposure from BTS.

label: Rail
description: Rail transport. No current source mapping assigns this mode.

label: Transit
description: Public transit systems. No current source mapping assigns this mode.

label: Marine
description: Waterborne transport. No current source mapping assigns this mode.

label: Pipeline
description: Pipeline transport. No current source mapping assigns this mode.
